items.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022
items.q: of course I would love to sound like Mike but nobody’s going to sound like Mike and I don’t — I keep trying to practice and be as good as him

ctx.x: You’ve got an impressive — I guess we’d call it a discography so far, with your own material and playing on other people’s recordings. Do you have a sense of why people call you to play on their recordings?

Well you know wooh, that’s a good one. Well you know with Randy yes it’s my husband and I’m the wife, but clearly if I couldn’t — you know a lot of people assume oh if she’s in the Brecker Brothers and plays with him, yes and no. Yes I’m the wife but clearly if I couldn’t play I wouldn’t be there. And I think he likes the idea that I have my own sounds and of course I would love to sound like Mike but nobody’s going to sound like Mike and I don’t — I keep trying to practice and be as good as him but I wanted to…
I like that, you have something to say. I know that some of the older generation of musicians they used to say well tell a story when you’re improvising.
